```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| echo: false

library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

This page compares the meteorological data sources available for Lake Rotorua, describes what each one brings to the model forcing built in [`climate-scenario-workflow.qmd`](climate-scenario-workflow.qmd), and documents the data-quality issues this comparison has caught along the way (a rainfall unit mismatch, a doubled wind-unit conversion on the buoy, ERA5 "drizzle", and a drifting buoy humidity sensor). See [`data.qmd`](data.qmd) for full source/access details on every dataset in the pipeline, including these five.

## Download the data

[**Download rotorua_met_data.zip**](downloads/rotorua_met_data.zip) (\~29 MB) contains the lake and reanalysis meteorology used on this page. The Rotorua Airport data (NIWA and MetService) are not included.

| File | Contents | Period | Resolution |
|------------------|------------------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `buoy_met.csv` | Lake buoy meteorology, old (2007–22) and new (2022–) loggers, with a `logger` column | Jul 2007 – Oct 2026 | 15-minute (old buoy), hourly (new buoy) |
| `era5_hourly_original.csv` | ERA5-Land hourly meteorology as read by the pipeline (`era5_hourly_met`) | Jan 1988 – Dec 2025 | Hourly |
| `era5_hourly_bias_corrected.csv` | ERA5 after bias correction against the buoy and the MetService airport, with derived variables (`era5_corrected_hourly`) | Jan 1988 – Dec 2025 | Hourly |
| `metadata.csv` | One row per file and column: description, units, time zone, time resolution and processing notes | – | – |

All timestamps are local clock time at a fixed UTC+12 offset (NZST, `Etc/GMT-12`, no daylight saving). Units follow the AEME `MET_*` convention (for example temperature in °C, pressure in Pa, wind in m/s, rain in m per record, shortwave in W/m²); the `metadata.csv` has the full list. Buoy relative humidity is raw and unreliable after 2024; see the humidity discussion below before using it.

## The five sources

| Source | Target(s) | Record | What it measures | Where it's strong | Where it's weak |
|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|
| **Lake buoy** | `all_buoy_met_data` = `old_buoy_met_hr_aeme` (2007–22) + `rotorua_buoy_met_aeme_hr` (2022–present) | 2007–present (\~19 yr, two loggers) | On-lake met station: temp, RH, wind, pressure, rain; shortwave radiation on the new buoy only | The only source actually measured *over the lake surface* — the ground truth for lake-effect corrections. The two loggers agree closely where they can be compared (see below), so they splice into one record | Old buoy has no shortwave radiation; \~15% of hourly records missing for some variables; rain gauge is noisy |
| **Airport (NIWA #1770)** | `niwa_met_hourly_aeme` | 1981–2025 (44 yr) | Nominally a full met suite at a fixed land station | Longest record; good temperature/RH | Wind and radiation have little or no overlap with the buoy window; daily rain is incomplete (\~250 mm/yr); land-station bias vs. the lake |
| **Airport (MetService NZROA)** | `airport_met_aeme` (from `airport_met`) | Jan 1993 – Jun 2023 (30 yr) | Hourly temp, RH, station pressure, rain, shortwave radiation, wind speed and direction | Complete, independent hourly record with a real rain gauge, shortwave and wind; overlaps the old buoy for 16 years | Ends June 2023; wind, rain and radiation are *hour-ending* values; station pressure missing for \~32 % of hours; land station |
| **ERA5-Land (reanalysis)** | `era5_hourly_met` | 1988–Dec 2025 (38 yr) | Gridded reanalysis, full met suite | Continuous, gap-free, extends into the future for scenario work | Coarse grid cell (not lake-specific); its own biases need correcting against real observations |
| **PC10 / BOPRC stations** | `pc10_climate_met` | Temp/RH: 2006–present (Edmund Rd); Rain: **1901–present** (Whakarewarewa) | Temp, RH, rain only — no radiation or wind | Rain record is by far the longest of any source here; independent of NIWA's instrumentation | No radiation/wind; weaker correlation with the buoy than the airport (see comparison below) |

The airport and PC10 stations were chosen from BOPRC/NIWA's larger station networks by longest, most complete overlapping record rather than by raw distance to the lake — see [the PC10 extraction notes](targets.qmd) for the full station comparison (`pc10_climate_station_summary()`); for Lake Rotorua, every realistic candidate station already sits close to the lake, so record length matters more than the last kilometre of proximity.

## Comparing the raw sources against the buoy

`met_source_comparison` aggregates all five sources to daily values and scores the NIWA airport, MetService airport, ERA5 and PC10 against the buoy — the only source with a direct claim to being "true" lake conditions — over whatever window each pair overlaps, for temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed, shortwave radiation and station pressure. Since the old buoy data were added (`all_buoy_met_data`), that window reaches back to **mid-2007**, so most comparisons rest on up to \~16 years of daily pairs.

::: callout-note
**Wind units.** Buoy wind is in m/s and is extrapolated to 10 m (from 2 m on the new buoy and 1.5 m on the old one). A duplicated knots→m/s conversion was being applied to buoy wind that was already in m/s, scaling it by 0.514; it was removed in `buoy_to_aeme_met()` (and the old-buoy equivalent) in October 2026. Before the fix the buoy's mean 10 m wind was \~2.8 m/s; it is now \~5.4 m/s. That change moves ERA5's apparent wind bias from \~−0.2 m/s to \~−2.8 m/s, so **every wind result on this page reflects the corrected series**, and earlier versions of this page that reported a small ERA5 wind bias were wrong. Separately, the buoy's own rain had a unit bug, fixed in `rotorua_buoy_met_data`: before 2023-10-23 it logged rain in mm/10 min, while later records use mm.

```{r}
#| label: comparison-stats
#| echo: false

cmp <- tar_read(met_source_comparison)
cmp$stats |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
              caption = "Daily bias/MAE/RMSE/r of each source vs. the buoy, computed only over days both series have valid data.")
```

```{r}
#| label: comparison-plot
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Daily air temperature, relative humidity, rainfall and wind speed from all five sources, over the buoy's record (2007–present)."

tar_read(met_source_comparison_plot)
```

**What this shows** (ERA5 now covers 1988–2025, so ERA5 comparisons span the whole buoy record, 2007–2025):

-   **Air temperature** — every land/reanalysis source reads colder than the buoy: NIWA airport −0.95 °C, MetService airport −0.92 °C, PC10 −1.00 °C and ERA5 −1.47 °C on daily means. The offset is stable year to year (ERA5 − buoy is −1.2 to −1.7 °C in every full year 2007–2025), so it is a real and consistent difference between lake-surface air and land/grid-cell air rather than drift. ERA5 tracks the buoy's day-to-day shape best (r ≈ 0.99); both airports follow at r ≈ 0.98; PC10 is weakest (r ≈ 0.86, MAE ≈ 1.9 °C).
-   **Relative humidity** — all sources read more humid than the buoy: ERA5 +7.0 %, NIWA airport +6.4 %, MetService +6.1 %, PC10 +3.1 %. This is *not* simply a lake effect: the land station and ERA5 agree with each other (hourly ERA5 − MetService is +1.6 % over 1993–2023), and the buoy's offset is not constant — the annual ERA5 − buoy RH bias is +2–3 % in 2022–23, +9.5 % in 2024, +13 % in 2025 and +48 % in the 2026 data (buoy mean RH 47 %). **The buoy RH sensor looks drifty or faulty, particularly from 2024 on** (see the hourly section). PC10 RH has very weak correlation with the buoy (r ≈ 0.32).
-   **Rainfall** — mean daily totals agree well. The MetService gauge matches the buoy almost exactly (bias ≈ 0, **r ≈ 0.86**, the best rain agreement of any source), ERA5 is next (bias ≈ 0, r ≈ 0.76), then the NIWA airport (r ≈ 0.59, biased low because its daily rain is incomplete), and PC10 is essentially uncorrelated day to day (r ≈ 0.06) despite agreeing on long-run totals — consistent with real small-scale spatial variability in rain rather than a PC10 error.
-   **Wind speed** — the buoy (10 m) averages \~5.4 m/s, well above every other source: MetService airport −1.7 m/s (r ≈ 0.89), NIWA airport −2.1 m/s (r ≈ 0.82, only 679 days), and **ERA5 −2.9 m/s (r ≈ 0.89, 6,071 days), i.e. about 53 % below the buoy**. Even against the land MetService station ERA5 is \~1.1 m/s low on matched hours, so ERA5 under-reads wind generally and the buoy is windier than both land stations (open-water fetch plus the 2 m → 10 m extrapolation). PC10 has no wind station.
-   **Shortwave radiation** — only the MetService airport (r ≈ 0.97, bias −5 W/m² over 469 days of overlap with the new buoy, Feb 2022–Jun 2023) and ERA5 (r ≈ 0.84, bias −10 W/m² over 1,404 days) can be compared; the NIWA airport has no overlap with the buoy.
-   **Station pressure** — all sources differ from the buoy by a nearly constant offset (r ≥ 0.996): MetService −0.13 kPa, ERA5 −1.10 kPa and NIWA airport +3.29 kPa. MetService (station height 285 m) is by far the closest.

## Hourly comparison: buoys, MetService airport and ERA5

The daily comparison scores sources against a single combined buoy series. This section looks at hourly resolution and brings in four series: the old buoy (2007–22), the new buoy (2022–), ERA5 (1988–2025), and the MetService airport record (1993–Jun 2023), which is the only independent, complete hourly station in the set and overlaps the old buoy for 16 years. ERA5 now covers the whole MetService record, so ERA5 − MetService statistics below use 30 years (\~265,000 hours) rather than 12. The section answers three questions the daily view cannot: **(1) can the two buoy loggers be treated as one record?**, **(2) what are ERA5's biases on matched hours, variable by variable, including shortwave, pressure and wind direction?** and **(3) is the buoy itself a trustworthy reference for each variable?** The old and new buoys never overlap in time, so they are compared with each other through their distributions and indirectly through ERA5 and MetService.

All series are floored to the hour (the old buoy logs every 15 minutes, so the `:00` record is kept) and duplicate hours are dropped, keeping the first value so wind direction is never averaged arithmetically. MetService rain, wind and radiation are hour-*ending* values (they describe the hour preceding the stamp); MetService wind is the hourly mean where recorded and the 10-minute mean otherwise.

```{r}
#| label: hourly-setup

era5_hourly_met          <- tar_read(era5_hourly_met)
airport_met_aeme         <- tar_read(airport_met_aeme)
old_buoy_met_hr_aeme     <- tar_read(old_buoy_met_hr_aeme)
rotorua_buoy_met_aeme_hr <- tar_read(rotorua_buoy_met_aeme_hr)

dfs <- list(
  "Buoy (new, 2022-)"   = rotorua_buoy_met_aeme_hr,
  "Buoy (old, 2007-22)" = old_buoy_met_hr_aeme,
  "ERA5"                = era5_hourly_met,
  "MetService airport"  = airport_met_aeme
)

# Variables shared by at least two sources (missing ones are filled with NA)
vars <- c("MET_tmpair", "MET_prsttn", "MET_wndspd", "MET_humrel",
          "MET_radswd", "MET_pprain", "MET_wnddir")

var_labels <- c(
  MET_tmpair = "Air temperature (°C)",
  MET_prsttn = "Station pressure (Pa)",
  MET_wndspd = "Wind speed (m/s)",
  MET_humrel = "Relative humidity (%)",
  MET_radswd = "Shortwave radiation (W/m²)",
  MET_pprain = "Rain (check units!)",
  MET_wnddir = "Wind direction (°)"
)

cols <- c("Buoy (new, 2022-)"   = "#1b9e77",
          "Buoy (old, 2007-22)" = "#d95f02",
          "ERA5"                = "#7570b3",
          "MetService airport"  = "#e7298a")

prep <- function(df) {
  for (v in setdiff(vars, names(df))) df[[v]] <- NA_real_
  out <- df |>
    mutate(Date = lubridate::floor_date(Date, "hour")) |>
    select(Date, all_of(vars)) |>
    arrange(Date)
  distinct(out, Date, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

dfs_h <- purrr::map(dfs, prep)

met_all <- dfs_h |>
  bind_rows(.id = "source") |>
  mutate(source = factor(source, levels = names(dfs)))

met_long <- met_all |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = vars, labels = var_labels[vars]))

lin_vars <- setdiff(vars, c("MET_wnddir", "MET_pprain"))  # linear, non-rain
lin_long <- met_long |> filter(variable %in% var_labels[lin_vars])

# Timezone of each series (ERA5 starting at 13:00 hints at a UTC vs NZ offset)
tibble::tibble(
  source = names(dfs),
  tzone  = sapply(dfs, \(d) attr(d$Date, "tzone")),
  start  = do.call(c, lapply(dfs_h, \(d) min(d$Date))),
  end    = do.call(c, lapply(dfs_h, \(d) max(d$Date)))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Timezone attribute and extent of each hourly series.")
```

### Summary statistics

Full-record statistics for each source. Differences here can partly reflect the different years and seasons each record samples, so the matched-hour comparison further down is the fairer test of bias.

```{r}
#| label: hourly-summary

summary_stats <- met_all |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(lin_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(variable, source) |>
  summarise(
    n_obs  = sum(!is.na(value)),
    pct_NA = round(100 * mean(is.na(value)), 1),
    mean   = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd     = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    p05    = quantile(value, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95    = quantile(value, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    min    = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max    = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n_obs > 0)

knitr::kable(summary_stats, digits = 2,
             caption = "Hourly summary statistics by variable and source (full record of each).")
```

**The two buoy loggers are statistically interchangeable for temperature, wind and pressure.** Mean air temperature (14.0 °C both), 10 m wind speed (5.45 vs 5.34 m/s) and pressure (98.34 kPa both) match to within about 2 %, so there is no sign of a step change at the 2022 handover, and ERA5's matched-hour offsets for these variables are nearly identical against each logger (below). Relative humidity is the exception (see the annual-bias table). Full-record means for ERA5 are not directly comparable with the buoys because ERA5 spans 1988–2025, but they show the same character: ERA5 is cooler (12.2 °C, SD 4.6 vs 14.0 °C, SD 4.0), more humid (mean 83 % vs 75 %; median 87 % vs 77 %) and much less windy (2.51 vs \~5.4 m/s). The MetService airport sits in between on wind (3.58 m/s), is cooler than the buoys (12.7 °C, with a much wider range of −5 to 30 °C), is more humid (81 %), and reads 98.20 kPa station pressure (the buoys 98.34 kPa). Shortwave means agree across the three sources that measure it (new buoy 165, ERA5 169, MetService 167 W/m²).

### Is the buoy a stable reference? Annual bias by year

Because ERA5 and the MetService airport are independent of the buoy and of each other, year-by-year bias against them shows whether a buoy sensor has drifted. A real, physical offset (such as lake vs. land air temperature) should be steady; sensor drift should not.

```{r}
#| label: hourly-annual-bias

b_all <- bind_rows(dfs_h[["Buoy (old, 2007-22)"]], dfs_h[["Buoy (new, 2022-)"]])
era5_h <- dfs_h[["ERA5"]]
ms_h   <- dfs_h[["MetService airport"]]

yr_bias <- function(ref, test, v, lab) {
  inner_join(select(ref, Date, ref = all_of(v)),
             select(test, Date, test = all_of(v)), by = "Date") |>
    filter(!is.na(ref), !is.na(test)) |>
    mutate(yr = lubridate::year(Date)) |>
    group_by(yr) |>
    summarise(bias = mean(test - ref), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(comparison = lab, variable = v)
}

annual_bias <- bind_rows(
  yr_bias(b_all, era5_h, "MET_tmpair", "ERA5 - buoy"),
  yr_bias(b_all, era5_h, "MET_humrel", "ERA5 - buoy"),
  yr_bias(b_all, era5_h, "MET_wndspd", "ERA5 - buoy"),
  yr_bias(ms_h,  era5_h, "MET_tmpair", "ERA5 - MetService"),
  yr_bias(ms_h,  era5_h, "MET_humrel", "ERA5 - MetService"),
  yr_bias(ms_h,  era5_h, "MET_wndspd", "ERA5 - MetService")
) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = vars, labels = var_labels[vars]))

annual_bias |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = comparison, values_from = bias) |>
  arrange(variable, yr) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Annual mean hourly bias of ERA5 against the buoys and against the MetService airport.")

ggplot(annual_bias, aes(yr, bias, colour = comparison)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("ERA5 - buoy" = "#1b9e77", "ERA5 - MetService" = "#e7298a")) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Annual ERA5 bias vs. buoy and vs. MetService airport",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean bias (ERA5 - reference)", colour = NULL)
```

**Temperature and wind offsets are steady; the RH offset is not.** ERA5 − buoy temperature stays between −1.2 and −1.7 °C in every full year 2007–2025 (−2.1 °C in the partial 2026 data), and ERA5 − MetService stays between −0.3 and −0.8 °C across all 31 years, so those are stable properties of the sources. ERA5 − buoy wind is −2.6 to −3.4 m/s every year. ERA5 − MetService wind is steadier in sign but drifts from about −0.8 to −1.0 m/s in the 1990s to −1.3 to −1.5 m/s in 2019–2023, so part of the ERA5 wind deficit against the land station has grown over time (a MetService sensor or ERA5 change, not the buoy). ERA5 − MetService RH is typically +0 to +2.5 %, but larger in the mid-1990s (+7 to +9 % in 1994 and 1996), which is the one place the land record disagrees with ERA5. Against the buoy, the RH bias is +3.6 to +5.2 % in 2007–10, wanders from +5 % to +9.5 % through 2011–2020, falls to +2–3 % in 2022–23, then rises to +9.5 % (2024), +13 % (2025) and +48 % in 2026, when the buoy reports a mean RH of only 47 %. That pattern points to calibration drift or a failing sensor rather than a lake effect.

### Distributions

The ECDF is the most useful view for spotting shifts (a horizontal offset between curves is a bias) and differences in the tails (e.g. ERA5's dampened wind extremes).

::: panel-tabset
## Density

```{r}
#| label: hourly-density
#| fig-height: 7

ggplot(lin_long, aes(value, fill = source, colour = source)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.25, adjust = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) + scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Met variable distributions", x = NULL, y = "Density",
       fill = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

## ECDF

```{r}
#| label: hourly-ecdf
#| fig-height: 7

ggplot(lin_long, aes(value, colour = source)) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Empirical CDFs", x = NULL, y = "F(x)", colour = NULL)
```

## Boxplots

```{r}
#| label: hourly-box
#| fig-height: 7

ggplot(lin_long, aes(source, value, fill = source)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.1, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Boxplots", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```
:::

### Rainfall

Rainfall is zero-inflated, so it is compared by wet-hour fraction and by the distribution of non-zero hours rather than by mean and SD alone.

All four series are now in the same unit (m/hour — the old buoy's maximum is 0.046 m/hr and the MetService maximum 0.047 m/hr, in line with the others), so no rescaling is needed; `rain_scale` is kept at 1 as a hook in case that changes.

```{r}
#| label: hourly-rain

rain_scale <- c("Buoy (new, 2022-)"   = 1,
                "Buoy (old, 2007-22)" = 1,
                "ERA5"                = 1,
                "MetService airport"  = 1)    # edit once units are confirmed

rain <- met_all |>
  filter(!is.na(MET_pprain)) |>
  mutate(rain = MET_pprain * rain_scale[as.character(source)])

rain |>
  group_by(source) |>
  summarise(
    n_obs        = n(),
    wet_fraction = mean(rain > 0),
    mean_all     = mean(rain),
    mean_wet     = mean(rain[rain > 0]),
    p95_wet      = quantile(rain[rain > 0], 0.95),
    max          = max(rain),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5, caption = "Hourly rainfall summary by source (units as stored).")

rain |>
  filter(rain > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(rain, colour = source)) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Non-zero rainfall ECDF (log x-axis)", x = "Rain (as stored)",
       y = "F(x)", colour = NULL)
```

**ERA5 gets the rain total right but not its character.** Mean hourly rain is similar across sources (≈ 0.00014–0.00018 m/hr), but ERA5 is "wet" in **41 % of hours versus 12–16 % on both buoys and the MetService gauge**, and its wet hours are weaker (mean 0.42 mm/hr vs 0.9–1.3 mm/hr; 95th percentile 2.0 vs 4.5–5.5 mm/hr; maximum 21 vs 28–47 mm/hr). That is the classic reanalysis drizzle pattern — light rain spread over too many hours with extremes smoothed away. The two buoys and the independent MetService gauge agree with each other, which is strong evidence that the buoy rain gauge is not the problem. For lake forcing this matters mostly for event-scale inflow and extremes; daily and longer totals are fine.

### Wind direction

Wind direction is circular, so it is shown as wind roses and summarised with a circular mean (and mean resultant length, $\bar R$: 0 = no preferred direction, 1 = all hours from one direction) rather than a plain mean or density.

```{r}
#| label: hourly-wind-rose
#| fig-height: 4.5

met_all |>
  filter(!is.na(MET_wnddir)) |>
  ggplot(aes(MET_wnddir)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count / sum(count))),
                 binwidth = 22.5, boundary = 0, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 360), breaks = seq(0, 315, 45),
                     labels = c("N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW")) +
  coord_polar(start = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ source) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Wind direction frequency", x = NULL, y = "Proportion of hours")

met_all |>
  filter(!is.na(MET_wnddir)) |>
  group_by(source) |>
  summarise(
    circ_mean = (atan2(mean(sin(MET_wnddir * pi / 180)),
                       mean(cos(MET_wnddir * pi / 180))) * 180 / pi) %% 360,
    Rbar      = sqrt(mean(sin(MET_wnddir * pi / 180))^2 +
                       mean(cos(MET_wnddir * pi / 180))^2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Circular mean wind direction (°) and mean resultant length by source.")
```

### Matched-hour comparison: ERA5, MetService and the buoys

To remove sampling differences between periods, series are paired on hours where both have valid data: ERA5 against each buoy, ERA5 against the MetService airport, and MetService against each buoy. Bias is the second-named series minus the first-named reference, i.e. ERA5 − buoy, ERA5 − MetService, and MetService − buoy, so a negative wind bias means the first series reads low.

```{r}
#| label: hourly-paired

paired <- function(ref, test, vars) {
  inner_join(
    ref  |> select(Date, all_of(vars)),
    test |> select(Date, all_of(vars)),
    by = "Date", suffix = c("_ref", "_test")
  ) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-Date, names_to = c("variable", "which"),
                        names_pattern = "(.*)_(ref|test)$", values_to = "value") |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = which, values_from = value) |>
    filter(!is.na(ref), !is.na(test))
}

pair_vars <- c("MET_tmpair", "MET_prsttn", "MET_wndspd", "MET_humrel",
               "MET_radswd", "MET_wnddir")

pairs_all <- bind_rows(
  list(
    "ERA5 vs new buoy" = paired(dfs_h[["Buoy (new, 2022-)"]],   dfs_h[["ERA5"]], pair_vars),
    "ERA5 vs old buoy" = paired(dfs_h[["Buoy (old, 2007-22)"]], dfs_h[["ERA5"]], pair_vars),
    "ERA5 vs MetService" = paired(dfs_h[["MetService airport"]], dfs_h[["ERA5"]], pair_vars),
    "MetService vs new buoy" = paired(dfs_h[["Buoy (new, 2022-)"]], dfs_h[["MetService airport"]], pair_vars),
    "MetService vs old buoy" = paired(dfs_h[["Buoy (old, 2007-22)"]], dfs_h[["MetService airport"]], pair_vars)
  ),
  .id = "pair"
)

pairs_all |>
  filter(variable != "MET_wnddir") |>
  group_by(pair, variable) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    bias = mean(test - ref),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((test - ref)^2)),
    r    = cor(ref, test),
    ks_D = unname(suppressWarnings(ks.test(ref, test)$statistic)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
               caption = "Matched-hour bias (ERA5 − buoy), RMSE, correlation and Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance.")

# Wind direction: signed angular difference in (-180, 180]
pairs_all |>
  filter(variable == "MET_wnddir") |>
  mutate(d = ((test - ref + 180) %% 360) - 180) |>
  group_by(pair) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_diff = mean(d), mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(d)), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Wind direction: signed (ERA5 − buoy) and absolute angular difference (°).")
```

**What the matched hours show:**

| Variable | ERA5 − new buoy | ERA5 − old buoy | ERA5 − MetService | MetService − new / old buoy | Reading |
|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|
| Air temperature | −1.56 °C (r 0.96) | −1.44 °C (r 0.96) | −0.56 °C (r 0.96) | −1.00 / −0.91 °C (r 0.93 / 0.94) | ERA5 is close to the land station; the buoy is warmer than both |
| Relative humidity | +6.9 % (r 0.73) | +6.9 % (r 0.83) | +1.6 % (r 0.77) | +0.6 / +6.7 % (r 0.92 / 0.89) | ERA5 ≈ MetService; the buoy RH disagrees and changes over time (see annual bias) |
| Wind speed | −2.92 m/s (r 0.76) | −2.87 m/s (r 0.70) | −1.09 m/s (r 0.76) | −1.58 / −1.73 m/s (r 0.84 / 0.74) | ERA5 reads \~53 % below the buoy and \~30 % below the land station |
| Shortwave | +9 W/m² (r 0.91) | — | +2 W/m² (r 0.95) | −5.5 W/m² (r 0.95; new buoy only) | Good everywhere; ERA5 matches MetService almost exactly |
| Station pressure | −1.10 kPa (r 0.997) | −1.11 kPa (r 0.998) | −0.97 kPa (r 0.998) | −0.09 / −0.14 kPa (r ≥ 0.999) | Near-perfect shape; constant elevation-type offset for ERA5 |
| Wind direction | +5° bias, 46° mean abs. diff. | −3°, 60° | +1°, 39° | +15° / −4°, 42° / 62° | ERA5 gets the prevailing flow, not hourly direction; the old buoy's direction is the least consistent |

The comparison that matters most for the humidity result is the second column pair: the new buoy and the MetService airport agree on RH over their 2022–23 overlap (+0.6 %), the old buoy and MetService do not (+6.7 %), and ERA5 agrees with MetService to within about 2 % over 30 years. The buoy's RH is therefore the odd one out, not ERA5.

Wind roses agree on the prevailing flow (circular mean 247°, 255°, 254° and 237° for the new buoy, old buoy, ERA5 and MetService — WSW–W throughout). Directional concentration is similar for the new buoy and ERA5 ($\bar R$ = 0.21 and 0.24) but weaker for the old buoy (0.13) and the MetService airport (0.11), which may reflect a different sensor or exposure rather than a different wind climate.

### Diurnal cycle

The mean diurnal cycle is also a quick check for timestamp conventions: if the sources' radiation peaks at different hours, their clocks or averaging conventions differ (the timezone table above shows what each `Date` column is stored in).

```{r}
#| label: hourly-peak-hour

met_all |>
  filter(!is.na(MET_radswd)) |>
  mutate(hour = lubridate::hour(Date)) |>
  group_by(source, hour) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(MET_radswd), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(source) |>
  slice_max(mean, n = 1) |>
  select(source, peak_hour = hour, peak_mean_Wm2 = mean) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Hour of peak mean shortwave radiation, by source.")
```

Mean shortwave peaks at hour 12 on the new buoy but hour 13 in ERA5 and the MetService airport. All four `Date` columns carry the same fixed-offset timezone (`Etc/GMT-12`, NZST, no daylight saving), so this is not a timezone mismatch in the stored data. ERA5 and MetService values are hour-*ending* (they describe the preceding hour), whereas the buoy stamp is instantaneous or hour-centred, so the series are offset by roughly 30–60 minutes. The lag table below shows the effect on hourly skill is small, but it is worth knowing for sub-daily radiation work.

```{r}
#| label: hourly-lag

lag_r <- function(ref, test, v, k) {
  t2 <- test
  t2$Date <- t2$Date - k * 3600
  d <- inner_join(select(ref, Date, a = all_of(v)), select(t2, Date, b = all_of(v)), by = "Date")
  d <- filter(d, !is.na(a), !is.na(b))
  cor(d$a, d$b)
}

lag_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  variable = c("MET_radswd", "MET_tmpair"),
  pair = c("new buoy vs ERA5", "new buoy vs MetService", "ERA5 vs MetService"),
  lag_h = -2:2
)
lag_grid$r <- purrr::pmap_dbl(lag_grid, \(variable, pair, lag_h) {
  ref  <- switch(pair, "ERA5 vs MetService" = dfs_h[["ERA5"]], dfs_h[["Buoy (new, 2022-)"]])
  test <- switch(pair, "new buoy vs ERA5" = dfs_h[["ERA5"]], dfs_h[["MetService airport"]])
  lag_r(ref, test, variable, lag_h)
})

lag_grid |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = lag_h, values_from = r, names_prefix = "lag ") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Hourly correlation after shifting the second series by 0, ±1 and ±2 hours (positive lag = second series shifted later).")
```

```{r}
#| label: hourly-diurnal
#| fig-height: 6

met_all |>
  mutate(hour = lubridate::hour(Date)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(c("MET_tmpair", "MET_wndspd", "MET_humrel", "MET_radswd")),
                      names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  group_by(source, variable, hour) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = vars, labels = var_labels[vars])) |>
  ggplot(aes(hour, mean, colour = source)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Mean diurnal cycle (hour as stored in Date)", x = "Hour", y = NULL,
       colour = NULL)
```

## A real bug this comparison caught

Running this comparison surfaced a unit mismatch that a single-source sanity check would have missed: **ERA5-Land's raw `MET_pprain` column is stored in mm/hour, while every other source in this pipeline (buoy, airport, PC10) is in m/hour/m-day**, the AEME convention. Uncorrected, ERA5's rainfall was reading roughly 1000x too high in the shared units (mean 0.18 vs. the buoy's 0.0008 m/hr) — and because `era5_bias_correction` originally excluded `MET_pprain` from correction (rainfall was assumed to be a poor target due to buoy-gauge reliability, not a units problem), that inflated value would have flowed straight through `era5_corrected_hourly` into every scenario baseline.

Fixed in two places:

1.  [**`read_era5_hourly_met()`**](https://github.com/tadhg-moore/rotorua-pc10/blob/main/R/scenario_climate_workflow.R) now converts `MET_pprain` mm/hour → m/hour at read time, so the fix applies everywhere the ERA5 series is used, not just here.
2.  **`MET_pprain` is now included** in both `era5_bias_correction` and `era5_bias_correction_extended`'s `vars`, using the same `method = "scale"` day-of-year correction as the other variables — see the comparison above for why this is reasonable (no evidence of a buoy under-catch, just noise), while still treating the buoy's rain series with more caution than its temperature/RH/wind.

```{r}
#| label: era5-pprain-skill
#| echo: false

bc <- tar_read(era5_bias_correction)
bc$skill |>
  filter(variable == "MET_pprain", stage %in% c("cv_raw", "cv_corrected")) |>
  mutate(kind = ifelse(grepl("raw", stage), "raw ERA5", "bias-corrected")) |>
  select(variable, kind, n, bias, mae, rmse, r, kge) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4,
              caption = "Leave-one-year-out cross-validated skill for MET_pprain specifically, before vs. after the scale correction (post unit-fix).")
```

*Note: the pipeline now quantile-maps rain before this fit (see "Fixing ERA5 rainfall"), so the `raw` rows for `MET_pprain` here and in the table below are the quantile-mapped series, and the skill shown is the second-stage monthly scale.* With the units fixed, ERA5 rain now agrees with the buoys on mean totals (hourly r ≈ 0.52 overall). The scale correction leaves rain essentially unchanged — cross-validated KGE is marginally *lower* after correction (0.31 vs 0.34) — which is the expected outcome for a variable whose mismatch is in timing and intensity rather than in the mean. Rain correction is harmless but should not be credited with improving the forcing.

## How well does bias correction fix ERA5?

The comparisons above are all of *raw* ERA5. `era5_bias_correction` fits a day-of-year scale correction of ERA5 against the combined buoy record; the leave-one-year-out cross-validated skill below shows how much of the raw offsets it removes on held-out years.

```{r}
#| label: era5-skill-all
#| echo: false

bind_rows(
  bc$skill |> mutate(reference = "buoy"),
  tar_read(era5_humrel_correction)$skill |> mutate(reference = "MetService airport")
) |>
  filter(stage %in% c("cv_raw", "cv_corrected")) |>
  mutate(kind = ifelse(grepl("raw", stage), "raw ERA5", "bias-corrected")) |>
  select(variable, reference, kind, n, bias, rmse, r, kge) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
              caption = "Cross-validated ERA5 skill, raw vs. bias-corrected, against the combined buoy record (all variables except humidity) and the MetService airport (humidity).")
```

-   **Wind is now the largest correction**: bias −2.88 → 0.00 m/s, RMSE 3.59 → 2.11 m/s and KGE 0.18 → 0.71, with correlation unchanged (r ≈ 0.72) — a scale correction fixes the mean, not the hourly timing error visible in the matched-hour scatter.
-   **Temperature and pressure improve a lot**: temperature bias −1.48 → 0.00 °C and RMSE 2.01 → 1.34 °C; pressure bias −1,105 Pa → 0 and RMSE 1,107 → 57 Pa.
-   **Humidity** is fit to the MetService airport (`airport_met_aeme`, \~260,000 matched hours, 1993–Jun 2023) rather than the buoy, as a separate stage in front of `era5_bias_correction` (target `era5_humrel_correction`). Raw ERA5 already agrees with that station to within about 2 % (bias +1.6 %, r 0.77), so the correction is small: cross-validated RMSE 10.0 → 9.9 %, KGE 0.765 → 0.766, and the mean bias goes to zero (mean ERA5 RH 82.9 % → 81.3 %). It is essentially a bias removal, not a skill improvement.
-   **Shortwave**: already close to unbiased (+9 W/m²); correction gives only a small gain, and it is fit on the new buoy alone (\~30,000 hours).
-   **Rain**: no gain from `scale` (above). Quantile mapping followed by a monthly scale does fix wet-hour frequency and intensity — see the next subsection.

### Fixing ERA5 rainfall: quantile mapping vs. scaling

The default `method = "scale"` rain correction is only a monthly multiplier on totals, so it cannot touch the drizzle problem found above. `metscale::fit_met_bias_correction()` also offers empirical quantile mapping (`"eqm"`) and quantile delta mapping (`"qdm"`), which remap the whole ERA5 distribution — zeros included — onto the buoy distribution month by month. Four ERA5 rain variants are compared here, all fit against `all_buoy_met_data`:

-   **raw** — uncorrected ERA5.
-   **scale** — the current `era5_bias_correction` approach (monthly multiplier).
-   **eqm** — quantile mapping (100 quantiles), which also adjusts wet-hour frequency and intensity.
-   **eqm+scale** — `eqm`, then a second monthly `scale` fit on the `eqm` output to put the total back on the buoy's.

`qdm` was also fitted and gives numbers identical to `eqm` on the historical period (it only differs when extrapolating a trend), so it is not shown separately.

```{r}
#| label: rain-fit

all_buoy_met_data <- tar_read(all_buoy_met_data)

fit_rain <- \(e, m) metscale::fit_met_bias_correction(
  e, all_buoy_met_data, vars = "MET_pprain", method = m,
  nquantiles = 100, verbose = FALSE)
apply_rain <- \(e, f) metscale::apply_met_bias_correction(e, f, verbose = FALSE)

f_scale <- fit_rain(era5_hourly_met, "scale")
f_eqm   <- fit_rain(era5_hourly_met, "eqm")
e_eqm   <- apply_rain(era5_hourly_met, f_eqm)
f_es    <- fit_rain(e_eqm, "scale")

rain_variants <- list(
  raw         = era5_hourly_met,
  scale       = apply_rain(era5_hourly_met, f_scale),
  eqm         = e_eqm,
  `eqm+scale` = apply_rain(e_eqm, f_es)
)

# Cross-validated (leave-one-year-out) skill. For eqm+scale this is the
# second-stage fit only (scored against the eqm output); the first-stage
# skill is in the "eqm" row.
bind_rows(
  raw         = f_scale$skill |> filter(stage == "cv_raw"),
  scale       = f_scale$skill |> filter(stage == "cv_corrected"),
  eqm         = f_eqm$skill   |> filter(stage == "cv_corrected"),
  `eqm+scale` = f_es$skill    |> filter(stage == "cv_corrected"),
  .id = "method") |>
  select(method, n, rmse, r, kge) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4,
               caption = "Cross-validated hourly rain skill vs. the buoy (m/hr). Hourly RMSE and r *worsen* with quantile mapping while KGE improves, because a more realistic intermittent series is penalised for timing errors.")
```

```{r}
#| label: rain-hourly-compare

fl <- \(d) d |>
  mutate(Date = lubridate::floor_date(Date, "hour")) |>
  distinct(Date, .keep_all = TRUE) |> select(Date, MET_pprain)
j <- fl(all_buoy_met_data) |> rename(obs = MET_pprain) |> filter(!is.na(obs))
for (n in names(rain_variants)) {
  v <- fl(rain_variants[[n]])
  j[[n]] <- v$MET_pprain[match(j$Date, v$Date)]
}
j <- filter(j, !is.na(raw))
vv <- c("obs", names(rain_variants))
cmp_names <- c(obs = "Buoy", raw = "ERA5 raw", scale = "ERA5 scale",
               eqm = "ERA5 eqm", `eqm+scale` = "ERA5 eqm+scale")

hourly_tab <- purrr::map_dfr(vv, \(x) {
  y <- j[[x]]
  tibble::tibble(
    series = cmp_names[[x]],
    wet_fraction_pct = 100 * mean(y > 0),
    mean_wet_mm_hr = 1000 * mean(y[y > 0]),
    p95_wet_mm_hr = 1000 * quantile(y[y > 0], 0.95),
    max_mm_hr = 1000 * max(y),
    total_mm_yr = 1000 * mean(y) * 8766,
    r_hourly = if (x == "obs") NA_real_ else cor(j$obs, y))
})
knitr::kable(hourly_tab, digits = 2,
             caption = "Matched hours (ERA5 variants vs. buoy): wet-hour fraction, wet-hour intensity and annual total.")

j |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(vv), names_to = "series", values_to = "rain") |>
  filter(rain > 0) |>
  mutate(series = factor(cmp_names[series], levels = cmp_names)) |>
  ggplot(aes(rain * 1000, colour = series)) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "#7570b3", "#9e9ac8", "#d95f02", "#1b9e77")) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(title = "Non-zero hourly rain: ERA5 variants vs. buoy",
       x = "Rain (mm/hr, log axis)", y = "F(x)", colour = NULL)
```

**On matched hours,** `scale` leaves the drizzle exactly where it was (41.4 % wet hours vs. 15.0 % on the buoy) and slightly weakens the extremes (maximum 16.9 vs. 46 mm/hr). `eqm` brings wet-hour fraction (15.3 %), mean wet-hour intensity (1.15 vs. 1.06 mm/hr), 95th percentile (5.7 vs. 5.2 mm/hr) and maximum into line with the buoy, but preserves ERA5's \~10 % high total (1,542 vs. 1,396 mm/yr). **`eqm+scale` gets both**: 15.3 % wet hours, 1.04 mm/hr mean wet intensity, 5.2 mm/hr p95 and 1,399 mm/yr, with cross-validated KGE of 0.46 against 0.33 for raw ERA5 and 0.30 for the plain `scale` correction.

#### Cross-check against independent gauges

Because the corrections are fit to the buoy, the buoy cannot also validate them. The same variants are therefore scored at daily resolution against the buoy, the NIWA airport, the MetService airport and PC10 gauges (daily totals in mm), and at hourly resolution against the MetService gauge, which is the only fully independent hourly rain record.

```{r}
#| label: rain-daily-crosscheck

dv <- purrr::map(rain_variants, \(d) d |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date)) |>
  group_by(Date) |>
  summarise(v = sum(MET_pprain, na.rm = TRUE) * 1000, .groups = "drop"))

w <- tar_read(met_source_comparison)$wide |>
  filter(variable == "MET_pprain") |>
  transmute(Date, buoy = buoy * 1000, airport = airport * 1000,
            metservice = metservice * 1000, pc10 = pc10 * 1000)
for (n in names(dv)) w[[n]] <- dv[[n]]$v[match(w$Date, dv[[n]]$Date)]

ref_names <- c(buoy = "Buoy", airport = "Airport (NIWA)", metservice = "MetService airport",
               pc10 = "PC10")
daily_tab <- purrr::map_dfr(names(ref_names), \(ref) {
  d <- filter(w, !is.na(.data[[ref]]), !is.na(raw))
  purrr::map_dfr(c(ref, names(rain_variants)), \(x) {
    y <- d[[x]]
    tibble::tibble(
      reference = ref_names[[ref]],
      series = if (x == ref) paste(ref_names[[ref]], "(reference)") else paste("ERA5", x),
      n_days = nrow(d),
      wet_day_pct = 100 * mean(y >= 1),
      total_mm_yr = mean(y) * 365.25,
      p95_mm_day = quantile(y, 0.95),
      p99_mm_day = quantile(y, 0.99),
      max_mm_day = max(y),
      r = if (x == ref) NA_real_ else cor(d[[ref]], y))
  })
})
knitr::kable(daily_tab, digits = 2,
             caption = "Daily rain (mm/day) of ERA5 variants vs. each gauge, on days both have data. Wet day = ≥ 1 mm.")
```

-   **Buoy:** `eqm+scale` matches the buoy's annual total (1,397 vs. 1,393 mm/yr), p95 (20.2 vs. 20.2 mm/day) and maximum (278 vs. 281 mm/day); raw ERA5 has 44 % wet days against the buoy's 27 %, and the `eqm`-based variants 24–25 %. The upper tail is slightly over-stretched (p99 70 vs. 62 mm/day).
-   **MetService airport (independent hourly gauge)** is the strongest check, because it shares no instrument with the buoy. Over its 1993–2023 record it reads **1,397 mm/yr** on matched days (11,059 days); on matched hours its wet-hour fraction is 12.0 %, mean wet-hour rain 1.33 mm/hr and p95 5.0 mm/hr. `eqm+scale` gives 15.1 %, 1.01 and 5.0 mm/hr and a total of 1,342 mm/yr, i.e. **\~4 % below MetService**, whereas raw ERA5 is 9 % above it (1,528 mm/yr, 41 % wet hours, 0.42 mm/hr wet-hour intensity). At daily resolution `eqm+scale` approaches the MetService p95 (19.6 vs. 21.2 mm/day) but under-counts wet days (24.4 % vs. 32.6 %) and over-stretches the extreme tail (p99 70 vs. 52 mm/day; maximum 232 vs. 167 mm/day). The shortfall arises because the correction is fit to the 2007–2025 buoy record while MetService covers 1993 onward, so any difference between the early (1993–2006) ERA5 and the buoy-era ERA5 is not corrected.
-   **PC10 (Whakarewarewa gauge)** reads 1,449 mm/yr over 13,880 days, so `eqm+scale` (1,340) is \~8 % below it and raw ERA5 (1,535) 6 % above. Its p95 (20.5 mm/day) is close to `eqm+scale` (19.6). PC10's wet-day fraction (37 %) is the highest of the gauges, but a once-daily reading probably smears wet days across two calendar days and inflates the count. Its daily correlation with ERA5 is very low in every case (r ≈ 0.05–0.10), as in the source comparison above. Together the buoy, MetService and PC10 bracket the true Rotorua total at roughly 1,400–1,450 mm/yr, with raw ERA5 sitting 6–12 % above all three.
-   **NIWA airport:** this check remains **unreliable**. Its daily rainfall averages only about 920 mm/yr on days it is "valid" — roughly a third below every other gauge — so its rain series appears incomplete (many days probably contain only some of the 3-hourly observations) and cannot be used to judge totals or wet-day frequency. The MetService record now fills that role.
-   **Daily skill:** all `eqm` variants have slightly lower daily correlation than `scale` or raw ERA5 against the buoy (r 0.75 vs. 0.76), consistent with the hourly double penalty.

```{r}
#| label: rain-hourly-metservice

ms <- fl(airport_met_aeme) |> rename(obs = MET_pprain) |> filter(!is.na(obs))
for (n in names(rain_variants)) {
  v <- fl(rain_variants[[n]])
  ms[[n]] <- v$MET_pprain[match(ms$Date, v$Date)]
}
ms <- filter(ms, !is.na(raw))
purrr::map_dfr(c("obs", names(rain_variants)), \(x) {
  y <- ms[[x]]
  tibble::tibble(
    series = if (x == "obs") "MetService (reference)" else paste("ERA5", x),
    n_hours = nrow(ms),
    wet_fraction_pct = 100 * mean(y > 0),
    mean_wet_mm_hr = 1000 * mean(y[y > 0]),
    p95_wet_mm_hr = 1000 * quantile(y[y > 0], 0.95),
    max_mm_hr = 1000 * max(y),
    total_mm_yr = 1000 * mean(y) * 8766,
    r_hourly = if (x == "obs") NA_real_ else cor(ms$obs, y))
}) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = "Hourly rain: ERA5 variants vs. the MetService airport gauge (independent of the buoy), matched hours.")
```

**Recommendation (now implemented in the pipeline):** use **`MET_pprain = "eqm"` followed by a monthly `scale`** for the historical ERA5 baseline. That fixes drizzle frequency, wet-hour intensity and the bulk of the tail and keeps the total on the buoy. The land gauges read 4–8 % higher than the corrected series (MetService −4 %, PC10 −8 %), and raw ERA5 reads 6–12 % higher than all three, so the corrected total is probably a slight underestimate rather than an overestimate. Because the second stage is fit on the output of the first, it needs two chained calls rather than a single `method =` vector:

In `_targets.R` this is `era5_rain_eqm_correction` → `era5_hourly_met_rainqm` (stage 1), then `era5_bias_correction` fitted on `era5_hourly_met_rainqm` (stage 2, together with the other variables), with `era5_corrected_hourly` and `era5_corrected_daily_baseline` built from `era5_hourly_met_rainqm`. The equivalent standalone code is:

```{r}
#| label: rain-recommended
#| eval: false

# 1. quantile-map rain onto the buoy distribution
bc_rain_eqm <- metscale::fit_met_bias_correction(
  era5_hourly_met, all_buoy_met_data, vars = "MET_pprain",
  method = "eqm", nquantiles = 100, verbose = FALSE)
era5_eqm <- metscale::apply_met_bias_correction(era5_hourly_met, bc_rain_eqm)

# 2. restore the buoy's total with a monthly ratio
bc_rain_scale <- metscale::fit_met_bias_correction(
  era5_eqm, all_buoy_met_data, vars = "MET_pprain",
  method = "scale", by = "doy-loess", verbose = FALSE)
era5_rain_corrected <- metscale::apply_met_bias_correction(era5_eqm, bc_rain_scale)
```

::: callout-note
**`expand_met()` rounding (fixed).** `metscale::expand_met()` previously rounded every column to 3 decimals. Rain is in m/hr, so that quantised it to whole millimetres: in testing it cut the corrected wet-hour fraction from 15.2 % to 4.9 % and erased all the drizzle correction (and coarsened earlier `era5_corrected_hourly` rain). It now rounds to 6 decimals and the pipeline calls `apply_met_bias_correction(expand = TRUE)` directly. `era5_corrected_daily_baseline` rounds daily totals to 6 decimals too, so it is unaffected.
:::

Caveats: hourly timing is unchanged (r stays ≈ 0.5) — this corrects the *distribution*, not when rain falls. The quantile map caps ERA5 extremes at the buoy's observed maximum, and the extreme daily tail ends up somewhat heavier than the MetService gauge shows.

## How this improves lake model forcing

1.  **The buoy reference is now \~19 years, not \~4.5, and ERA5 now spans 1988–2025.** Adding the old buoy lets the day-of-year corrections in `era5_bias_correction` and `niwa_to_buoy_bias_correction` train on \~140,000 hourly pairs instead of \~40,000, and the hourly comparison shows the two loggers agree on temperature, wind and pressure. The longer ERA5 record also overlaps the whole MetService record, so ERA5 can now be checked against an independent station for 30 years.
2.  **Caught a forcing bug before it reached the model.** The ERA5 rain unit error above would have meant every ERA5-driven scenario — including every future GCM projection, since deltas are applied to the ERA5 baseline — ran with rainfall roughly 3 orders of magnitude too high. A single-source pipeline has no way to notice this; comparing independent sources does.
3.  **Wind is the largest bias in the forcing, and it is now correctly sized.** With the doubled unit conversion removed, ERA5 reads \~2.9 m/s (\~53 %) below the buoy's 10 m wind, not \~0.2 m/s. Wind drives mixing and surface heat flux directly, so `era5_bias_correction`'s `MET_wndspd` scale correction (cross-validated RMSE 3.59 → 2.11 m/s, KGE 0.18 → 0.71) is one of the most consequential steps in the pipeline. The land stations cannot substitute: the MetService airport also reads 1.7 m/s below the buoy, so the correction really is a land/reanalysis → lake transfer and depends on the buoy's 2 m/1.5 m → 10 m extrapolation being right.
4.  **The buoy → airport extension now supports every variable it needs.** `niwa_to_buoy_bias_correction` trains on the buoy overlap (2007–present) and cuts NIWA-airport-vs-buoy RMSE from 2.02 → 1.74 °C (temperature); wind is corrected for bias (−2.3 → −0.1 m/s) with a modest RMSE gain (3.18 → 2.94 m/s, r ≈ 0.63), while humidity, which uses the 2022–23 buoy only in this fit, shows no cross-validated gain (RMSE 5.7 → 6.6 %). Because ERA5 now reaches back to 1988, `era5_bias_correction_extended` has far more paired data than before (\~140,000–165,000 hours for temperature, humidity and wind) and cuts ERA5 RMSE for temperature from 2.08 → 1.45 °C, wind from 4.26 → 2.51 m/s (KGE 0.10 → 0.65), and humidity from 7.3 → 7.0 %.
5.  **A second, independent hourly station is now available.** The MetService airport record (1993–Jun 2023) has a real rain gauge, shortwave and wind, and agrees with ERA5 on temperature (−0.6 °C), humidity (+1.6 %) and shortwave (+2 W/m²). It validates the rain correction independently of the buoy, exposes the buoy RH drift, supplies the humidity correction, and is a candidate for extending reference records back before 2007 (for variables where it agrees well with the buoy: temperature, pressure, rain).
6.  **PC10's 1901–present rainfall record is the longest available context for Rotorua rainfall**, over 40 years longer than the airports'. That's directly useful for `summarise_climate_extremes.R` / [`climate-extreme-events.qmd`](climate-extreme-events.qmd)'s historical-extremes framing, and as a long-run independent check on whatever ERA5 rainfall climatology ends up driving the historical baseline and scenario deltas. Its weak daily correlation with the buoy for RH and rain (r ≈ 0.32 and 0.06) means it shouldn't be used as a `fit_met_bias_correction()` reference for those variables.
7.  **Wind direction and shortwave timing check out.** ERA5 reproduces the prevailing WSW–W flow (hourly mean absolute direction error \~39–60°) and the shortwave daily cycle (r = 0.91 against the new buoy and 0.95 against MetService), so ERA5-derived direction and radiation are defensible for the model.

## Caveats

-   **Buoy relative humidity is not a reliable reference, so ERA5 humidity is corrected against the MetService airport instead.** The old buoy (2007–22) reads \~4–9.5 % below ERA5 and the MetService airport, and the new buoy's offset drifts from +2–3 % in 2022–23 to +9.5 % (2024), +13 % (2025) and +48 % in 2026 (mean RH 47 %). `era5_bias_correction` therefore no longer corrects `MET_humrel`; `era5_humrel_correction` fits it to `airport_met_aeme` (1993–Jun 2023, so the fit covers ERA5 up to Jun 2023), and the correction is applied before the buoy-based one. `buoy_met_fit_ref` keeps buoy RH only for 2022-01-01 to 2023-12-31 for the remaining buoy-referenced fits (`niwa_to_buoy_bias_correction` and, through it, `era5_bias_correction_extended`, which still corrects humidity against that lake-equivalent series). `all_buoy_met_data` and the comparisons above still include all buoy RH. The airport station is a land station, so any lake effect on humidity (the buoy is the only lake-surface sensor) is not captured; the airport fit assumes the same land–lake humidity relationship ERA5 already has. ERA5 also runs 7–9 % more humid than MetService in 1994 and 1996, so the early-1990s ERA5 humidity deserves caution.
-   **Station pressure (`MET_prsttn`).** The buoys log sensible station pressure (\~98.3 kPa on both loggers; the MetService airport 98.2 kPa). ERA5 reads a near-constant **1.1 kPa lower** (r = 0.997), a grid-cell elevation difference of order 100 m, not a units error; the NIWA airport reads \~3.3 kPa *higher*. All offsets are removed by the scale corrections (ERA5 RMSE falls to \~57 Pa), but raw ERA5 and NIWA pressures should not be used uncorrected.
-   **`era5_bias_correction_extended` radiation and wind reference caveats.** Its shortwave reference is the NIWA airport's radiation, which has no overlap with the buoy and so is *not* put through the buoy transfer function (`niwa_to_buoy_bias_correction` has no radiation model), and its wind reference is only weakly corrected (r ≈ 0.63 with the buoy). Prefer `era5_bias_correction` for `MET_wndspd` and `MET_radswd`. The comment in `_targets.R` that describes only 2 wind pairs and 0 radiation pairs predates the old buoy and the longer ERA5 and is worth updating.
-   **Shortwave is validated on limited data.** The old buoy has no shortwave, the NIWA airport has none that overlaps the buoy, and the MetService airport overlaps the new buoy only from Feb 2022 to Jun 2023 (\~11,000 hours), so ERA5 shortwave rests on the new buoy (\~30,000 hours) plus that MetService overlap (ERA5 versus MetService shortwave over 1993–2023 agrees to +2 W/m², r 0.95).
-   **ERA5 wind deficit against MetService grows over time** (from \~−0.8 m/s in 1993 to \~−1.5 m/s in 2023), which the buoy-only wind correction cannot see. If wind drives a historical simulation before 2007, the early-period correction is likely too small.
-   **Sub-daily timing.** The buoy stamps are offset from ERA5/MetService hour-ending stamps by roughly 30–60 minutes (see the diurnal section). This matters for hourly radiation and temperature, not for daily results.
-   **ERA5 rain is wet too often** (41 % of hours vs 12–16 %) with weak hourly intensity; fine for totals, less so for event-scale extremes. The current `scale` rain correction does not address this; `eqm` followed by `scale` does (see "Fixing ERA5 rainfall"). `era5_bias_correction_extended` still uses plain `scale` for rain.
-   PC10 has **no radiation or wind data**, so `pc10_climate_met` is a partial forcing (temp/RH/rain only) — useful for comparison and historical context, not as a standalone forcing source.
-   **Hour-stamp de-duplication.** `prep()` in the hourly section drops a large number of duplicated hour stamps (first value kept); the old buoy's 15-minute rows are reduced to the `:00` record. This is harmless for the comparisons here but means sub-hourly information is not used.
